arxiv-2102-05180.title: Pulse interactions in weakly nonlinear coherent optical communication links
arxiv-2102-05180.creator: J Gibney 1, I A Kuk 2 and I R Gabitov 1,2
arxiv-2102-05180.description: Abstract The intrachannel interaction of pulses in weakly nonlinear coherent optical fiber lines is theoretically investigated. It is shown that the main contribution to the perturbation of the optical field comes from resonant interactions of ordered triplets of pulses. The structure of triplets is determined. The weight contributions of such interactions are calculated.

arxiv-2103-05080.title: No dimension reduction for doubling subsets of ℓ q \ell_{q} when q > 2 q>2 revisited Thanks: F. Baudier was partially supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant Number DMS-1800322.
arxiv-2103-05080.creator: F. Baudier, K. Swieçicki, A. Swift
arxiv-2103-05080.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by F. Baudier, K. Swieçicki, A. Swift. We revisit the main results from [ 4 , 5 ] and [ 20 ] about the impossibility of dimension reduction for doubling subsets of ℓ q \ell_{q} for q > 2 q>2 . We provide an alternative elementary proof of this impossibility result that combines the simplicity of the construction in [ 4 , 5 ] with the generality of the approach in [ 20 ] (except for L 1 L_{1} targets).

arxiv-2202-07035.title: Testing the Tools of Systems Neuroscience on Artificial Neural Networks
arxiv-2202-07035.creator: Grace W. Lindsay
arxiv-2202-07035.description: Abstract Neuroscientists apply a range of common analysis tools to recorded neural activity in order to glean insights into how neural circuits implement computations. Despite the fact that these tools shape the progress of the field as a whole, we have little empirical evidence that they are effective at quickly identifying the phenomena of interest.

arxiv-2308-12038.title: Large Multilingual Models Pivot Zero-Shot Multimodal Learning across Languages
arxiv-2308-12038.creator: Jinyi Hu, Yuan Yao, Chongyi Wang, Shan Wang, Yinxu Pan, Qianyu Chen Tianyu Yu Hanghao Wu Yue Zhao Haoye Zhang, Xu Han Yankai Lin Jiao Xue Dahai Li Zhiyuan Liu Maosong Sun
arxiv-2308-12038.description: Abstract Recently there has been a significant surge in multimodal learning in terms of both image-to-text and text-to-image generation. However, the success is typically limited to English, leaving other languages largely behind. Building a competitive counterpart in other languages is highly challenging due to the low-resource nature of non-English multimodal data (i.e., lack of large-scale, high-quality image-text data).

arxiv-2312-05905.title: Improving Subgraph-GNNs via Edge-Level Ego-Network Encodings
arxiv-2312-05905.creator: Nurudin Alvarez-Gonzalez nuralgon@gmail.com, Andreas Kaltenbrunner kaltenbrunner@gmail.com, Vicenç Gómez vicen.gomez@upf.edu
arxiv-2312-05905.description: Abstract We present a novel edge-level ego-network encoding for learning on graphs that can boost Message Passing Graph Neural Networks (MP-GNNs) by providing additional node and edge features or extending message-passing formats. The proposed encoding is sufficient to distinguish Strongly Regular Graphs, a family of challenging 3-WL equivalent graphs.

arxiv-2402-15180.title: Break the Breakout: Reinventing LM Defense Against Jailbreak Attacks with Self-Refinement
arxiv-2402-15180.creator: Heegyu Kim, Sehyun Yuk, Hyunsouk Cho, Department of Artificial Intelligence, Department of Software, Computer EngineeringAjou University, Suwon 16499, Republic of Korea {khk6435, sdfg8931, hyunsouk}@ajou.ac.kr
arxiv-2402-15180.description: Abstract Caution: This paper includes offensive words that could potentially cause unpleasantness. Language models (LMs) are vulnerable to exploitation for adversarial misuse. Training LMs for safety alignment is extensive and makes it hard to respond to fast-developing attacks immediately, such as jailbreaks.

arxiv-2506-16698.creator: Dinesh Ramasamy, Shakti Kumar, Chris Cadonic, Jiaxin Yang, Sohini Roychowdhury, Esam Abdel Rhman, Srihari Reddy
arxiv-2506-16698.description: Abstract . Sequence-based recommendations models are driving the state-of-the-art for industrial ad-recommendation systems. Such systems typically deal with user histories or sequence lengths ranging in the order of O( 10 3 10^{3} ) to O( 10 4 10^{4} ) events.

pmc-11347206.title: Antibiotic pharmacokinetics in infected pleural effusions
pmc-11347206.creator: David T Arnold, Liam Read, Oliver Waddington, Fergus W Hamilton, Sonia Patole, Jessica Hughes, Alice Milne, Alan Noel, Mark Bayliss, Nicholas A Maskell, Alasdair MacGowan
pmc-11347206.description: Pleural infection is usually treated with empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics, but limited data exist on their penetrance into the infected pleural space. We performed a pharmacokinetic study analysing the concentration of five intravenous antibiotics across 146 separate time points in 35 patients (amoxicillin, metronidazole, piperacillin-tazobactam, clindamycin and cotrimoxazole).

pmc-11431857.title: Deep Intraclonal Analysis for the Development of Vaccines against Drug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Lineages
pmc-11431857.creator: Ana Tajuelo, Eva Gato, Jesús Oteo-Iglesias, María Pérez-Vázquez, Michael J McConnell, Antonio J Martín-Galiano, Astrid Pérez, Jochen Mattner
pmc-11431857.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Despite its medical relevance, there is no commercial vaccine that protects the population at risk from multidrug-resistant (MDR) Klebsiella pneumoniae infections. The availability of massive omic data and novel algorithms may improve antigen selection to develop effective prophylactic strategies. Up to 133 exposed proteins in the core proteomes, between 516 and 8666 genome samples, of the six most relevant MDR clonal groups (CGs) carried conserved B-cell epitopes, suggesting minimized future evasion if utilized for vaccination.

pmc-11453804.creator: Alexandra Thibodeau, Christophe Richer dit Laflèche, Gérard Ngueta, Matea Belan, Farrah Jean-Denis, Marie-France Langlois, Marie-Helene Pesant, Belina Carranza Mamane, Jean-Patrice Baillargeon

Introduction: Infertility is a common problem that is affected by many lifestyle behaviors, and preconception lifestyle modifications are recommended in women with infertility and obesity.

pmc-11529518.title: Association between musculoskeletal sonographic features and response to treatment in patients with psoriatic arthritis
pmc-11529518.creator: Jessica Gutierrez, Sydney Thib, Sahil Koppikar, Richard J Cook, Lihi Eder
pmc-11529518.description: ABSTRACTObjectiveTo investigate the association between musculoskeletal sonographic features and clinical features, as well as treatment outcomes, in patients with active psoriatic arthritis (PsA).MethodsA prospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with active PsA. Disease activity was assessed clinically at baseline and 3–6 months after initiating therapy, with a Disease Activity Index for PsA (DAPSA) score calculated.

pmc-12405192.title: Perspective: Beyond the cherry on top: positioning nutrition where it belongs
pmc-12405192.creator: Francesca Tabacchi
pmc-12405192.description: As a dietitian, what drew me to cancer care was the impact that my role could have. I saw patients regain strength, tolerate chemotherapy better, or simply find a bit more comfort in an otherwise chaotic time. I saw how amazing a dietetic service in a free healthcare system can be.

pmc-12826818.title: Investigating the threat of AI to undergraduate medical school admissions: a study of its potential impact on the rating of applicant essays
pmc-12826818.creator: Joshua Choi, Jenny Zhao, Thuy-Anh Ngo, Lawrence Grierson
pmc-12826818.description: BackgroundMedical school applications often require short written essays or personal statements, which are purportedly used to assess professional qualities related to the practice of medicine. With generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools capable of supplementing or replacing inputs by human applicants, concerns about how these tools impact written assessments are growing.

pmc-13696663.title: PROMIS in routine clinical care: a scoping review of implementation and use
pmc-13696663.creator: Kyle Nolla, Merell Turner, George J Greene, Amy Sparling, Richard Gershon, Michelle Langer
pmc-13696663.description: PurposeThe Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS®) is a family of patient-reported outcome measures used in research and clinical practice, but little is known about its use in clinical care. This scoping review identified studies of PROMIS in routine clinical care to understand who is using PROMIS in routine clinical care and how.
